headline: Revenue surges but rising costs squeeze profit and EPS
summary_short: FTAI's Q2 2026 revenue was $953.1M, up 14.7% q/q and 40.9% y/y, but cost of sales grew faster, pulling pretax income down 11.0% q/q (25.9% y/y) and diluted EPS to $1.13 from $1.29 q/q and $1.57 y/y.
summary_long: Revenue rose to $953.1M (+14.7% q/q, +40.9% y/y), driven by Aerospace Products engine and module sales (CFM56-5B/-7B, V2500) and higher MRE contract sales to the 2025 Partnership, partly offset by lower lease, maintenance and asset-sales revenue as leased-asset counts fell. Cost of sales grew alongside product-sales volume, and operating expenses rose on compensation, logistics and technology costs, pulling pretax income to $150.7M (-$18.6M q/q, -$52.6M y/y) and diluted EPS to $1.13 (from $1.29 q/q, $1.57 y/y). Cash fell to $337.2M (-18.2% q/q) after $200.1M of H1 shareholder distributions; long-term debt was flat near $3.45B; equity was $404.0M. No forward guidance was disclosed.

drivers.explanation: Aerospace Products engine and module sales (CFM56-5B/-7B, V2500) and MRE contract sales to the 2025 Partnership drove y/y growth, partly offset by lower lease, maintenance and asset-sales revenue.
Cost of sales rose $266.5M y/y, primarily from higher CFM56 and V2500 engine and module sales volume; per the filing, cost growth tracked the aerospace revenue increase.
Operating expenses rose $33.2M y/y on higher compensation, logistics and technology-development costs, while other expense increased $36.9M on a smaller gain on sale to the 2025 Partnership.

Distributions to shareholders (dividends plus preferred-share redemptions) were $200.1M in H1 2026 versus $71.4M in H1 2025, per the filing's liquidity discussion, pulling cash down despite asset-sale proceeds.
Volume-driven revenue growth was offset by proportional cost growth and higher other expense, leaving pretax income and EPS lower than a year ago despite the top-line gain.
